svg.title: PA12 CF15: reported tensile strength at test temperatures
svg.desc: Six unconnected, equally sized dots at the six reported chamber conditions, with vertical capped whiskers for reported SD. Exact source values and condition-scoped counts are in the following table. Dot: reported central value. Vertical capped whisker: central value ± source-reported SD; n=3 tensile tests per condition. SD is not a confidence interval or a bound. Temperature uncertainty is unreported.
svg.text: PA12 CF15: reported tensile strength at test temperatures
Six discrete source summaries · one source-reported protocol · catalog only
Scientific wording and translations are machine-assisted and have not been independently scientifically or native-language reviewed.

g.text: Read before interpreting the plot or values
Six condition summaries from one study of horizontally FFF-printed Fiberlogy PA12 CF15 with alternating +45°/−45° raster. Same
source-reported protocol only; no cross-study or universal material claim. Shared metadata do not prove identical conditioning or
material invariance.
X is the reported chamber test condition after 30 minutes of stabilization. Actual specimen temperature and temperature uncertainty are
unreported. No x whiskers does not mean zero uncertainty; dot width does not show temperature precision.
Dots are reported central UTS values. The central statistic, aggregation, stress convention and stress-area basis are unknown; the
centers are not identified as means.
Vertical whiskers reproduce ± reported standard deviation (SD). Three tensile tests per condition are reported; raw replicates and their
independence are unverified. The SD formula is unknown. SD is not SEM, a confidence interval, an observed min–max range, a hard
bound, a coverage statement or a complete uncertainty budget.
Specific preparation, geometry and the 1 mm/min crosshead-rate protocol apply. Drying at 80 °C for 12 h does not establish measured
moisture; humidity/moisture are unknown. Declared 15 wt.% fibers and 100% infill do not establish measured composition or zero
porosity.
No interpolation, extrapolation, fitting, material prediction, ranking, design allowable or safety claim. Transcription/software checks
are not independent scientific validation. These summaries are not six independent confirmations.
Dot: reported central value. Vertical capped whisker: central value ± source-reported SD; n=3 tensile tests per condition. SD is not a
confidence interval or a bound. Temperature uncertainty is unreported.

svg.text: Reported conditions: only the six labeled points, 23–120 °C. Display margins 15–125 °C add no observations or validated range. Y display 0–55 MPa:
zero is a visual baseline, not an experimental bound. Whisker endpoints are central ± SD rendering arithmetic, not additional observations.
Table 3 source strings retain their trailing zeros. Printed digits do not establish resolution or accuracy. Record IDs and source-cell locators

Preparation, geometry and protocol
Source-reported nominal dog-bone geometry: length 150 mm; gauge length 80 mm; thickness 3 mm; narrow/wide widths 10/20 mm; grip
separation 110 mm. Crosshead-derived engineering strain uses the full 110 mm, including transition regions, not only the 80 mm gauge.
Local strain rate, dimensional tolerances and measured stress cross-section are unknown. No stress is reconstructed from geometry.
Creality K1 MAX FFF; horizontal build; alternating +45°/−45° raster; 100% linear infill; five contours; 0.2 mm layers; 0.6 mm
nozzle; nozzle/bed 265/100 °C; inner/outer wall speeds 60/60 mm/s; reported cooling 100%; reported specimen mass 6.42 g. Step-Lab
UD08 tension with integrated thermal chamber. Filament diameter 1.75 mm; supplied spool mass 0.5 kg.
Atmosphere and pressure are unknown. Numerical relative humidity, specimen moisture, temperature sensor location, stability tolerance,
and tensile heating rate are unknown. No DMA heating rate is transferred. Engineering-strain wording does not establish engineering
stress. ISO 527 is cited; compliance and the article-reported standard URL were not independently verified.
1 MPa = 1000000 Pa exactly. These are the same observations, not additional plotted records. Unit scaling adds no measurement precision and uses
no geometry or thickness.
Source, version and rights
Source: ciganas2026polym18050563
Selected Table 3 values: Ciganas, J.; Kalinauskis, T.; Cigane, U. (2026), Thermo-Mechanical and Fatigue Behavior of 3D-Printed PA12 CF15 for
Engineering Application, Polymers 18(5), 563, DOI 10.3390/polym18050563, CC BY 4.0. Reorganized into discrete observations with exact MPa-to-Pa
unit re-expression; source numbers and SD strings preserved; curator notes are original.
Publisher HTML inspected 3 October 2026, reported update 3 September 2026 02:53 CEST. PDF not inspected; no PDF-equivalence claim. The
cached/live discrepancy is in unselected Table 4. Only the six selected Table 3 UTS/SD cells agree across current HTML, visual inspection and a
second transcription; this is not experimental reproduction.
CC BY 4.0 adaptation: source numbers and SD strings preserved, reorganized and plotted as discrete condition summaries; SI units re-expressed;
curator notes are original. Publisher endorsement is not implied. Manufacturer Table 1 and source PDFs, figures, screenshots, HTML dumps and
raw measurements are excluded. MIT covers original project contributions and does not replace source rights.
Complete source/record snapshots, nulls, exact SI values and metadata digests remain in the JSON/CSV exports and HTML audit details.
SHA-256 values identify bundled catalog metadata, not original publisher artifact bytes. Full scientific snapshots and nulls are retained in the
JSON export.
